This likely happened when you were young:

You weren't able to recall ideas from books you were made to read in school

You were studying for an exam, but forgot everything before a test

Then teacher notices and drills this in your head:

"Reread it, and repeat it until it sticks"

As simple as that, now you've got memory all wrong.

An idea is planted: "If I can't memorize this by repetition, there's something wrong with me"

That's false.

You may forget where you leave things

You may even forget people's names..

Then you tell yourself these stories:

"I'm not good at remembering names...

I always forget them...

I'm a forgetful person..."

99% of the time, there's nothing wrong with your brain,

And being "forgetful" isn't a personality trait

This is also false.

And we're taught these false narrative since we're young

We take them as granted, never dare to question them and become self-fulfilling stories

The problem is we're taught passive learning as a default.

And we're measuring up to a standard that isn't even real!

"Moonwalking with Einstein" by Joshua Foer goes deeper into how memory actually works (and what your brain is capable of when you stop treating it like a hard drive).

Follow us (@collectivewisdomco) to read more and scroll less.

I do recall by speaking aloud after reading a paragraph or two. Helpful for me and less time consuming than writing.

sometimes i just sit here and think about all the things i could have done. all the potential wasted, all the opportunities missed because i was too scared, too lazy, too comfortable. it feels like a physical weight, this burden of unfulfilled potential. i see people my age crushing it, building empires, living their best lives, and im just... here. watching. wishing. and then i get mad at myself, promise to change, and the cycle repeats. its exhausting. i was so desperate for a way out, i started looking for anything. i saw a random comment on a forum, someone just casually dropped "your last excuse" by jace halden. i was like, fine, another book. but this one... this one was different. it didnt tell me what i wanted to hear, it told me what i needed to hear. it wasnt about motivation, it was about accountability. it made me realize that the only thing holding me back was me. and that was a hard pill to swallow. but it was also the most liberating thing. im still fighting that battle every day, but now i have a weapon. if you feel the weight of your own potential crushing you, maybe this book can help you pick it up.
We prefer not to remember all the books we've read. Just focus on feelings.
